title: Through Christ nearly all inherit one of three kingdoms of glory
setting: Joseph Smith returned from the Amherst conference and resumed revising the Bible at the John Johnson home in Hiram, Ohio. Sidney Rigdon was his scribe. Joseph had reasoned that heaven must hold more than one kingdom if people are judged by their deeds. On 16 February 1832, while pondering John 5:29, the two reported seeing a vision together. Philo Dibble later said about twelve men were in the room, but his accounts vary. The vision was printed in The Evening and the Morning Star in July 1832.
summary: The text opens with praise and a promise to reveal mysteries to the faithful. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon then testify that they saw the Son at the Father’s right hand. They report the fall of Lucifer and the fate of the sons of perdition, who alone are not redeemed. The vision describes the celestial glory, like the sun, for those who receive Christ’s testimony, are baptized, and overcome by faith. The terrestrial glory, like the moon, is for the honorable who were not valiant in that testimony. The telestial glory, like the stars, is for those who did not receive the gospel but did not deny the Holy Spirit. Its inhabitants are numberless, and all will bow to Christ. The writers say they saw more than they were allowed to write.

contextNote.title: The witness that comes before the kingdoms
contextNote.text: The vision began with a question about the resurrection in John 5:29. Before describing any kingdom, verses 20–23 record what the two men say they saw first: the Son at the Father’s right hand. Verse 22 states their testimony, given “last of all” after many others, that Christ lives. Verse 23 gives the basis: “we saw him” and heard a voice name him the Only Begotten. Verse 24 extends his role to the creation of worlds and their inhabitants. Verses 39–43 later make him the one through whom all but the sons of perdition are saved. In this passage, “testimony” means an eyewitness claim, and the rest of the vision builds on it.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for section 76 takes its title from verse 6 and centers on the vision’s witness of Christ. Comparing verses 51–53, 74–79, and 82–83, what separates each glory from the next?
reviewNote: Read all 119 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 16 February 1832, Joseph and Sidney, return from Amherst, and John 5:29. JSP historical introduction read: likely the upstairs room of the John and Alice (Elsa) Johnson home; Philo Dibble’s later and varying account of about twelve men present; July 1832 printing in The Evening and the Morning Star; mixed reception. Lucifer and Paul, Apollos, Cephas, etc. (vv. 26, 99–100) are not added as people since they appear as figures or claimed allegiances, not participants.
